title: Flying Cam Transition
description: A flying cam transition is one continuous flight that punches a wall or window and lands in a new room. Architecture becomes a tunnel; the join is travel, not a hidden cut.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Change rooms without a cut. Virtuoso intros, dreams, a house that is a mind: the camera flies a readable path through a named threshold and arrives.
A cut hidden by a passing truck is not this. Through-object uses a prop; this uses the building.
Geography has to stay readable or the stunt is only noise.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is an invisible cut on a dark frame. The tell: a pop into a new room with no travel through a hole.
The fix: fly through a named threshold and land; keep geography readable.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Flying Cam Transition in film?
A flying cam transition is one continuous flight that punches a wall or window and lands in a new room, changing spaces without a cut.
Flying Cam Transition vs Pass Through
Pass-through is the matter-optional path. Flying cam transition is specifically a flight that uses architecture as a tunnel and lands as a designed join.
When should I use Flying Cam Transition?
Use it to change rooms in one flight, for intros or dream geography. Do not use it as a default scene join.
How do I prompt Flying Cam Transition for AI image or video?
Write one flight through a named threshold into a new space. Example: Flying-cam transition through [Subject]'s world, one continuous flight that punches a wall or window and lands in a new room.
